text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Scottish soldier PATRICK LOGAN, who was killed by Aborigines while exploring the Brisbane River, was born in 1791. He was immortalised in the folksong "Moreton Bay".
English/Australian writer JOHN JAMES was born in 1843. He was known for "The Vagabond Papers"
Australian gold pioneer MARK HAMMOND, who survived typhoid and a scorpion bite, was born in 1844. He lost money in a hotel venture but found the world's finest gold reef at Hill End.
German general ERWIN ROMMEL, who was commander of the Afrika Corps in North Africa during World War Two, was born in 1891.
Australian rugby captain Sir NICHOLAS SHEHADIE was born in 1926. He was also a rugby administrator before accepting the position of Lord Mayor of Sydney.

British singer and actress PETULA CLARK was born in 1932. She started singing when she was nine and appeared in more than 20 films between 1944 and 1951. Her first hit was "The Little Shoemaker" in 1954. She became internationally known with "Downtown" in 1964. PETULA was one of the most popular female singers of the 1960s.

Swedish singer with 'Abba' ANNI-FRID LYNGSTAD was born in 1945. She was known as FRIDA with the group and is her solo singing career. Her one solo hit was "I Know There's Something Going On" in 1982 which was produced by PHIL COLLINS.
American/Australian actor CHRISTOPHER PATE, son of MICHAEL, was born in 1952. He had an extensive film and television career in the United States and Australia as an actor and a stuntman.
United State drummer with 'Chic' TONY THOMPSON was born in 1954. He has also been a session musician with performers such as MADONNA, ROBERT PALMER, MICK JAGGER and NILE RODGERS.
** EVENTS **
1777 : Congress adopted the Articles of Confederation of
perpetual union of the United States of America.
1901 : An electrical hearing aid was patented by MILLER
REESE of New York.
1918 : It was Victory Day in Great Britain. There were

unprecedented scenes as public rejoiced in the streets at the end of the first World War. For the first time in four years Big Ben struck one. Crowds gathered outside Buckingham Palace singing "God Save The King" and "Rule Britannia". Police turned a blind eye to the licensing kaws and allowed hotels to stay open.
1920 : The first meeting of the Assembly of the League
of Nations was held in Geneva.
1922 : The first scheduled broadcast was made from
Marconi House in London's Strand.
1935 : The MARX Brothers opened their comedy "A Night At
The Opera" in New York.
1956 : ELVIS PRESLEY's first film "Love Me Tender"
premiered in New York.
1968 : The largest passenger liner in the world, the

"Queen Elizabeth" docked at Southhampton at the end of her final voyage. She was launched in 1938 but war broke out before she could go into service. During the war she was based in Sydney as a troop carrier. Since her first commercial journey in 1946 she crossed the Atlantic hundreds of times.
1971 : Delegates from China took their seats at the
United Nations for the first time.
1985 : British prime minister MARGARET THATCHER and Irish
leader GARRETT FITZGERALD signed the Anglo-Irish agreement which gave the republic a consultative role in the running of Northern Ireland for the first time.
1991 : Brazilian President FERNANDO COLLOR DE MELLO
signed a landmark decree giving back the original lands of the Yanomami Indians.
1994 : In British soccer, Southampton star BRUCE
GROBBELAAR was charged over allegations that he had accepted bribes to fix matches.
